theory.title: Exercise 1.3.3: Should Be True/False - Boolean Logic
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 projects three holographic logic gates, each showing different boolean evaluations.

"PROTO-7, not all validations compare values. Sometimes you need to evaluate conditions—is the temperature safe? Are repairs complete? The Should Be True and Should Be False keywords handle boolean logic."

What are Boolean Assertions?

Boolean assertions validate that conditions evaluate to True or False. They're essential for:

  • Conditional checks: Is temperature below maximum?
  • State validation: Are repairs complete?
  • Logical expressions: Is count greater than threshold?
  • Flag verification: Is system online?

Should Be True

Validates that a condition or expression evaluates to True:

Should Be True    ${condition}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If condition is True → assertion passes
  • ❌ If condition is False → test fails

Should Be False

Validates that a condition or expression evaluates to False:

Should Be False    ${condition}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If condition is False → assertion passes
  • ❌ If condition is True → test fails

Boolean Constants

Robot Framework provides boolean constants:

*** Test Cases ***
Boolean Constants
    ${flag1}           Set Variable    ${True}      # Boolean True
    ${flag2}           Set Variable    ${False}     # Boolean False
    Should Be True     ${flag1}                     # ✅ PASSES
    Should Be False    ${flag2}                     # ✅ PASSES

Important: ${True} and ${False} are special Robot Framework variables (note the capital T and F).

Evaluating Expressions

The real power comes from evaluating Python-style expressions:

*** Test Cases ***
Expression Evaluation
    ${temp}            Set Variable    45
    ${max_temp}        Set Variable    50

    # Evaluate: is 45 < 50?
    Should Be True     ${temp} < ${max_temp}        # ✅ PASSES

Comparison Operators

OperatorMeaningExample
< Less than ${temp} < ${max}
> Greater than ${count} > ${min}
== Equal to ${status} == 'OK'
!= Not equal to ${error} != 'None'
<= Less than or equal ${value} <= 100
>= Greater than or equal ${score} >= 75

Numeric Comparisons

*** Test Cases ***
Temperature Check
    ${current_temp}    Set Variable    75
    ${max_safe}        Set Variable    100
    ${min_safe}        Set Variable    0

    Should Be True     ${current_temp} < ${max_safe}     # Below max
    Should Be True     ${current_temp} > ${min_safe}     # Above min
    Log                Temperature within safe range!

String Comparisons

For string comparisons, use quotes around the expected value:

*** Test Cases ***
Status Check
    ${status}          Set Variable    operational

    # String comparison - need quotes!
    Should Be True     '${status}' == 'operational'      # ✅ PASSES
    Should Be False    '${status}' == 'offline'          # ✅ PASSES

Logical Operators

Combine conditions with and, or, not:

*** Test Cases ***
Combined Conditions
    ${temp}            Set Variable    75
    ${pressure}        Set Variable    850

    # AND: both must be true
    Should Be True     ${temp} < 100 and ${pressure} < 1000

    # OR: at least one must be true
    Should Be True     ${temp} > 80 or ${pressure} > 900

    # NOT: negates condition
    Should Be True     not ${temp} > 100

Real-World Use Cases

1. Safety Threshold Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Safety Check
    ${radiation_level}    Set Variable    45
    ${safe_limit}         Set Variable    50

    Should Be True        ${radiation_level} < ${safe_limit}
    Log                   Radiation within safe limits

2. Status Flag Verification

*** Test Cases ***
System Status
    ${repairs_complete}    Set Variable    ${True}
    ${system_damaged}      Set Variable    ${False}

    Should Be True         ${repairs_complete}
    Should Be False        ${system_damaged}
    Log                    All systems operational

3. Range Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Value Range Check
    ${power_level}     Set Variable    65

    # Value must be between 50 and 100
    Should Be True     ${power_level} >= 50 and ${power_level} <= 100
    Log                Power level within operational range

Error Messages

When boolean assertions fail, the error shows the evaluated expression:

*** Test Cases ***
Failed Boolean Check
    ${temp}            Set Variable    110
    ${max}             Set Variable    100

    Should Be True     ${temp} < ${max}
    # ❌ ERROR: 110 < 100 should be true but was not

Custom Error Messages

Add custom messages for clarity:

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Message
    ${damage_count}    Set Variable    5
    ${max_allowed}     Set Variable    3

    Should Be True     ${damage_count} <= ${max_allowed}
    ...                msg=Damage count ${damage_count} exceeds maximum ${max_allowed}!

Failure Output:

AssertionError: Damage count 5 exceeds maximum 3!

Should Be True vs Numeric Assertions

AspectShould Be TrueShould Be Greater/Less Than
Syntax Should Be True ${x} < ${y} Should Be Less Than ${x} ${y}
Flexibility Any boolean expression Only comparisons
When to Use Complex conditions, logical operators Simple numeric comparisons
Example ${x} < ${y} and ${z} > 0 Compare two numbers

Advanced: Variable Type Checking

*** Test Cases ***
Type Validation
    ${value}           Set Variable    ${True}
    ${number}          Set Variable    42

    # Check if variable is boolean True
    Should Be True     ${value} is ${True}

    # Check if value is numeric
    Should Be True     isinstance(${number}, int)

Best Practices

1. Use Quotes for String Comparisons

*** Test Cases ***
String Comparison
    ${status}    Set Variable    OK

    # ✅ Correct: Quotes around strings
    Should Be True    '${status}' == 'OK'

    # ❌ Wrong: Without quotes may cause errors
    Should Be True    ${status} == OK

2. Simplify When Possible

*** Test Cases ***
Simplification
    ${flag}    Set Variable    ${True}

    # ❌ Redundant
    Should Be True    ${flag} == ${True}

    # ✅ Simpler
    Should Be True    ${flag}

3. Combine Related Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Combined Checks
    ${temp}        Set Variable    75
    ${pressure}    Set Variable    900

    # ✅ Good: One assertion for related conditions
    Should Be True    ${temp} < 100 and ${pressure} < 1000

    # Less efficient: Separate assertions
    Should Be True    ${temp} < 100
    Should Be True    ${pressure} < 1000

MENTOR-9: "Validate temperature and repair status. Create ${temp}=45, ${max_temp}=50, and verify temp is below max. Then create ${repairs_done}=${True} and validate it. Finally, create ${system_offline}=${False} and verify it's False. Show me you understand boolean logic."
